question: भारतीय संविधान में 'Concurrent List' के किसी विषय पर केंद्र और राज्य के कानून में टकराव होने पर क्या होता है?

options.text: राज्य का कानून प्रभावी होता है
अनुच्छेद 254 — केंद्र का कानून प्रभावी होता है (Repugnancy Rule) — परंतु राज्य को राष्ट्रपति की सहमति से अपवाद मिल सकता है
दोनों कानून समान रूप से प्रभावी होते हैं
Supreme Court तय करती है कि कौन-सा प्रभावी होगा

explanation: अनुच्छेद 254 — Repugnancy: Concurrent List पर Centre-State conflict → Central Law prevails (inconsistent state law void to extent of repugnancy)। Exception: यदि राज्य विधानमंडल ने कानून पारित किया और President ने assent दिया → state law prevails in that state। Health education (Concurrent List) → Central NHM guidelines vs State health education programs — central norms prevail, but states can add।

question: भारत में 'न्यायिक सक्रियता' (Judicial Activism) और 'न्यायिक संयम' (Judicial Restraint) के बीच tension को उदाहरण सहित समझाएँ।

options.text: Judicial Activism — केवल India में होती है

Judicial Activism: courts legislature/executive के domain में enter करती हैं (Right to Food case); Judicial Restraint: courts stay within constitutional role — tension: democratic accountability vs rights protection
Judicial Restraint — हमेशा बेहतर approach है
Judicial Activism — unconstitutional होती है

explanation: Judicial Activism examples: (1) Vishaka Guidelines (1997) — SC created sexual harassment law before Parliament, (2) PUCL v. Union — Right to Food → mid-day meals mandated, (3) MC Mehta cases — pollution enforcement. Judicial Restraint: Courts avoid policy decisions (Kesavananda — basic structure but not policy). Tension: Separation of powers vs rights vacuum. PIL mechanism enables activism. Health: SC orders on medical oxygen during COVID, free COVID vaccination PIL — judicial activism in health governance।

question: भारत में 'Cooperative Federalism' और 'Competitive Federalism' के बीच अंतर और स्वास्थ्य नीति में इनकी भूमिका क्या है?

options.text: दोनों एक ही हैं
Cooperative: Centre-State joint goals (NHM funding, SBCC); Competitive: states compete for investment/talent/rankings (Health Index) — दोनों health improvement में सहायक
Competitive Federalism — health में हानिकारक
India में केवल Cooperative Federalism है

explanation: Cooperative Federalism: Centre-State common agenda — NHM (60:40 funding), immunization campaigns, COVID response. Instruments: GST Council, Inter-State Council, NDC (now scrapped). Competitive Federalism: NITI Aayog's Health Index (rankings) → states compete on IMR, MMR, vaccination → best practices emerge. Kerala, TN consistently top rankings → policy diffusion. NITI's SDG India Index — similar. Health: both mechanisms work — cooperative for baseline, competitive for excellence।

question: भारत में 'सातवीं अनुसूची' की 'समवर्ती सूची' (Concurrent List) में स्वास्थ्य से संबंधित कौन-से प्रमुख विषय हैं?

options.text: समवर्ती सूची में स्वास्थ्य का कोई विषय नहीं
जनसंख्या नियंत्रण और परिवार नियोजन (Entry 20A), Education (Entry 25), drugs and poisons (Entry 19), forests (Entry 17-A)
सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य — Concurrent List में
समवर्ती सूची में केवल education है

explanation: Concurrent List health-related entries: (1) Entry 19 — 'Drugs and poisons' (drug regulation, CDSCO, pharmacies), (2) Entry 20A — 'Population control and family planning' (Family Welfare programs), (3) Entry 17A — Forests (tribal health linkage), (4) Entry 25 — Education (health education). State List Entry 6: Public health, sanitation, hospitals। Union List: Port quarantine (Entry 28)। This split → complex centre-state health policy।

question: 'Sarkaria Commission' (1983) और 'Punchhi Commission' (2007) ने Centre-State relations में स्वास्थ्य क्षेत्र के लिए क्या सिफारिशें दीं?

options.text: दोनों commissions ने health को ignore किया
दोनों ने Concurrent List items (family planning, drugs) में coordination mechanism strengthen करने, राज्यों की health autonomy respect करने की सिफारिश दी
दोनों commissions ने health को Union List में shift करने की सिफारिश की
Sarkaria Commission — health पर कोई view नहीं

explanation: Sarkaria Commission (1983-88): (1) Strengthen Inter-State Council for policy coordination, (2) Avoid misuse of Art. 356, (3) Governor's role reform, (4) Concurrent List — consultation before Central legislation. Punchhi Commission (2007-10): (1) Health as shared responsibility — more cooperative mechanisms, (2) States' fiscal capacity for health, (3) Central health schemes — State conditionalities should be flexible. Health implication: Both emphasized partnership model, not Central dominance in health policy।

question: भारत में 'Separation of Powers' के सिद्धांत और 'Checks and Balances' का स्वास्थ्य नीति में क्या महत्व है?

options.text: Separation of Powers — India में strictly maintained है

India में partial separation: Parliament legislates, Executive implements, Judiciary reviews — health में: legislation (PCPNDT), executive (NHM), judicial (Right to Health PILs) — all roles distinct but overlapping
India में Separation of Powers — US जैसा strict है
Checks and Balances — केवल political, health में irrelevant

explanation: India — partial separation (not strict like US): PM and Cabinet are part of both executive and legislature. Checks: (1) Parliament: questions, no-confidence, legislation, (2) Judiciary: judicial review, PIL, writs, (3) Constitutional bodies: CBI, CAG, EC. Health-specific checks: (1) Parliamentary Health Committee reviews health bills, (2) CAG audits NHM expenditures, (3) Supreme Court PILs on Right to Health, (4) CVC monitors drug procurement corruption. Without checks — health system accountability collapses।

question: भारत में 'संसदीय लोकतंत्र' (Parliamentary Democracy) और 'अध्यक्षात्मक लोकतंत्र' (Presidential Democracy) की तुलना करें और भारत की system की विशेषताएँ बताएँ।

options.text: India — presidential democracy है

Parliamentary: executive Legislature के प्रति जवाबदेह; Presidential: executive independent (US); India: Westminster Parliamentary model — but President elected indirectly, Supreme Court stronger than UK
India — mixed presidential-parliamentary है, constitution में defined
दोनों में कोई अंतर नहीं

explanation: Parliamentary features in India: (1) Collective ministerial responsibility to Lok Sabha, (2) PM from majority party, (3) President ceremonial (nominal executive), (4) Government's term depends on Lok Sabha confidence. Presidential features (US): (1) Fixed term, (2) Separate election, (3) Veto power, (4) No collective responsibility. India's unique features: (1) Written constitution, (2) Judicial review stronger than UK, (3) Federal character (state govts), (4) DPSP — social welfare constitutionalized. Health: Health Minister accountable to Parliament।

question: भारत में 'Public Interest Litigation' (PIL) के माध्यम से 'Right to Health' को किन महत्वपूर्ण न्यायिक निर्णयों ने आकार दिया?

options.text: PIL और Right to Health — असंबंधित
Paschim Banga (1996), PUCL v. Union (Right to Food), Parmanand Katara (emergency care), Devika Biswas (sterilization) — अनुच्छेद 21 के तहत health rights expand हुए
Right to Health — केवल 2017 MHCA से
PIL — Right to Health के लिए अनुचित mechanism है

explanation: Key health PILs: (1) Paschim Banga Khet Majoor Samity v. State (1996) — emergency medical care as Art. 21 right, (2) Consumer Education and Research Society — right to information about drugs, (3) Vincent Panikurlangara — right to free medicine, (4) PUCL — Mid-day meal, (5) Devika Biswas v. Union (2016) — sterilization deaths, right against negligent sterilization. Art. 21 (right to life) → right to health. SC has used PIL to direct governments on healthcare infrastructure, drug availability, emergency care।

question: भारत में 'Constitutional Morality' की अवधारणा और health rights में इसकी क्या भूमिका है?

options.text: Constitutional Morality — केवल sexual rights में
Supreme Court ने Constitutional Morality को popular morality से ऊपर रखा — LGBTQ+ health rights, Sabarimala, IPC 377 decriminalization — health equity implications
Constitutional Morality — Dr. Ambedkar की original concept नहीं
Constitutional Morality और popular morality — identical हैं

explanation: Dr. Ambedkar — Constitutional Morality: constitutional values trump popular sentiment. SC applications: (1) Navtej Johar (2018) — IPC 377 partially struck down: LGBTQ+ persons' dignity and health → Art. 21, (2) Sabarimala (2018) — women's equal access, (3) Right to Privacy (2017) — includes health data privacy. Health implications: (1) LGBTQ+ health services legally protected, (2) Trans rights → right to health, (3) Sexual and reproductive rights — constitutional morality basis. Popular morality cannot override constitutional health rights।

question: भारत में 'Direct Benefit Transfer' (DBT) ने स्वास्थ्य क्षेत्र में क्या परिवर्तन लाए हैं?

options.text: DBT — केवल LPG subsidy के लिए
Health DBT: JSY, JSSK, PMMVY, NHM incentives — Aadhaar-linked payment → leakage कम, beneficiary empowerment, real-time tracking
DBT — health sector में अप्रभावी है
DBT — केवल food subsidies में

explanation: DBT in Health (DBT Bharat portal): (1) JSY (Janani Suraksha Yojana) — institutional delivery incentive directly to mother's Aadhaar-linked account, (2) PMMVY — maternity benefit transfer, (3) ASHA incentives — direct transfer, (4) NHM scholarships — medical students, (5) PM-JAY — cashless claims to hospitals directly. Benefits: (1) Elimination of middlemen, (2) Reduces leakage, (3) Financial inclusion, (4) Real-time tracking। Challenges: (1) Aadhaar-health linkage exclusions, (2) Bank access in rural areas, (3) Network connectivity।

question: भारत में 'Decentralization' के तीन आयाम (3Ds) क्या हैं और स्वास्थ्य में इनका क्या महत्व है?

options.text: Devolution, Delegation, Deconcentration — केवल administrative theory
Decentralization (Rondinelli): Deconcentration (field offices), Delegation (parastatal), Devolution (local government) — health में: district health societies, Block PHCs, Gram Panchayat oversight
India में केवल Devolution है
Decentralization — health में counter-productive

explanation: Rondinelli's 3Ds: (1) Deconcentration — field offices of central agency (CMO, DCMO, Block Medical Officer — हिrarchy), (2) Delegation — parastatals (State Health Society, CMHO office), (3) Devolution — true local government power (Gram Panchayat over VHSNC). India's health decentralization: NRHM pushed devolution → District Health Society (DHS) with independent budget, Rogi Kalyan Samiti (hospital management committees). Benefits: local needs responsive, community accountability. Challenges: capacity, elite capture, corruption।

question: भारत में 'Right to Information Act 2005' का स्वास्थ्य जवाबदेही में क्या व्यावहारिक महत्व है?

options.text: RTI — health sector में अनुप्रयुक्त नहीं
PHC drug stock, ASHA payment records, inspection reports, tenders — सब RTI-able; patient's own medical records; hospital budget — transparency tool
RTI — केवल government ministers पर लागू
Medical records — RTI से exempt हैं

explanation: RTI in Health Applications: (1) PHC drug availability (stock registers), (2) ASHA incentive payment records, (3) Hospital inspection reports (fire safety, Bio-medical waste), (4) Drug tender documents, (5) NHM fund utilization, (6) Government hospital bed occupancy, (7) Patient's own medical records (if public hospital). Third Party Information — doctor's personal info protected. 2019 Amendment — weakens CIC but RTI right intact. NGO tool: PHRN (People's Health Rights Network) uses RTI extensively। Health accountability instrument।

question: भारत में 'Social Audit' (सामाजिक अंकेक्षण) किस प्रकार health programs में accountability सुनिश्चित करती है?

options.text: Social Audit — केवल MGNREGS में
Community members records verify करते हैं, public hearing में falsehood expose करते हैं — Gram Sabha की role; MGNREGS, NRHM, PDS, Midday Meal में applied
Social Audit — government द्वारा की जाती है
Social Audit — courts में होती है

explanation: Social Audit — MKSS (Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan) — Aruna Roy — pioneered in Rajasthan 1990s। Process: (1) Documents obtained (muster rolls, registers), (2) Community verification (who benefited?), (3) Jan Sunwai (public hearing) — discrepancies exposed, (4) Follow-up action. Health applications: (1) JSY/JSSK payments verification, (2) ASHA incentive misuse, (3) Hospital construction costs, (4) Drug procurement. 2011 amendment — Social Audit made mandatory for MGNREGS. Rajasthan — Social Audit Directorate. Tool for participatory accountability।

question: भारत में 'Pesa Act 1996' के section 4(m)(ii) में क्या प्रावधान है जो tribal health governance को प्रभावित करता है?

options.text: Gram Sabha को mining approve करने का अधिकार है
Gram Sabha को minor forest produce (सहित medicinal plants) का ownership — traditional healing resources पर समुदाय का अधिकार
Section 4(m) — education से related है
PESA में medicinal plants का कोई प्रावधान नहीं

explanation: PESA 1996, Section 4(m): Gram Sabha को ownership of minor forest produce। Minor Forest Produce (MFP) — includes medicinal plants, herbs। Significance: (1) Tribal healers (Vaidyas) maintain traditional medicine through this, (2) Community protection of medicinal plant resources, (3) Bio-piracy prevention, (4) Nagoya Protocol implementation. Health implications: (1) Traditional medicine continuation, (2) Bioversity of medicinal plants protected, (3) Economic returns from MFP → health expenditure capacity. Van Dhan Vikas Kendras — MFP value addition।

question: भारत में 'District Health Action Plan' (DHAP) तैयार करने की प्रक्रिया में political science के किन सिद्धांतों का अनुप्रयोग होता है?

options.text: DHAP — केवल medical officers prepare करते हैं
Participatory planning, Bottom-up approach, Needs-assessment with community, Multi-stakeholder convergence, Electoral accountability — DHAP एक political-technical document है
DHAP — top-down central mandate है
DHAP — non-political, purely technical है

explanation: DHAP (District Health Action Plan) — NHM framework। Political science dimensions: (1) Participatory planning (Gram Sabha inputs → Block → District), (2) Needs assessment — community health needs, (3) Multi-stakeholder: elected representatives (ZP), health officials, NGOs, (4) Public finance: district PIP (Program Implementation Plan), (5) Accountability: to State Health Society, (6) Democratic accountability: elected local bodies approve. DHAP = Technical health plan + Political process. CMO + CEOs + Zila Parishad + Community inputs। Annual planning cycle।

question: भारत में 'Rogi Kalyan Samiti' (RKS) / 'Hospital Management Society' किस अवधारणा के तहत आते हैं और इनकी health governance में क्या भूमिका है?

options.text: RKS — private hospital management के लिए
Community governance of public hospitals — locally managed, elected representatives + community + officials — Hospital revenue re-investment, patient welfare
RKS — केवल financial auditing करता है
RKS — केवल district hospitals में होती है

explanation: Rogi Kalyan Samiti (RKS) — registered society at PHC, CHC, District Hospital। NHM initiative for hospital community governance। Composition: elected MP/MLA/Panchayat representatives + officials (CMO, District Officer) + community members। Functions: (1) User fees management and re-investment, (2) Quality improvement, (3) Infrastructure maintenance, (4) Service monitoring, (5) Patient welfare. Democratic accountability mechanism: elected representatives in hospital governance. Untied funds → RKS discretion। Example: Madhya Pradesh, UP RKS successful models।

question: भारत में 'Disaster Management Act 2005' के section 35 और health preparedness में केंद्र की क्या भूमिका है?

options.text: DM Act 2005 में health का कोई mention नहीं

Section 35 — Central Government shall take all measures for effective implementation: national disaster management plan, guidelines, coordination with state agencies; NDMA health guidelines में pandemic preparedness
DM Act केवल natural disasters के लिए है
Health Emergency — अलग Act से manage होती है

explanation: DM Act 2005 — Section 35: Central Govt responsibilities including disaster management. NDMA → National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP). COVID-19 as 'notified disaster' under DM Act — enabled: (1) Lockdowns, (2) National directives overriding state autonomy partially, (3) NDRF deployment, (4) Economic packages. Health-specific: (1) NDMA COVID guidelines, (2) Hospital surge capacity, (3) Medical oxygen supply chain, (4) Vaccination as disaster response। Epidemic Diseases Act 1897 + DM Act 2005 — dual legal framework in COVID।

question: भारत में 'Gender Budgeting' (लिंग-उत्तरदायी बजट) का स्वास्थ्य क्षेत्र में क्या महत्व है?

options.text: Gender Budgeting — केवल women's welfare ministry के लिए
स्वास्थ्य बजट में महिलाओं और लड़कियों के specific health needs को अलग से allocate और track करना — gender-responsive health planning
Gender Budgeting — India में 2023 में शुरू हुई
Gender Budget — केवल education में relevant

explanation: Gender Budgeting — India से 2005 Union Budget में formally started। Health Gender Budget Statement: Part A (100% women-specific: JSY, Mahila Shakti Kendras) + Part B (30%+ women-benefiting schemes: Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan). Health-specific: (1) Maternal health funding tracking, (2) Nutrition for girls (POSHAN), (3) PCPNDT enforcement funds, (4) Women's mental health. Gender-disaggregated data in HMIS। UN Women support। SDG 5 (Gender Equality) + SDG 3 (Health) nexus।

question: भारत में 'Epidemic Diseases Act 1897' की सीमाएँ और 'New Public Health Bill' की आवश्यकता क्यों है?

options.text: Epidemic Diseases Act 1897 — COVID में पर्याप्त था
1897 Act — colonial, narrow (only epidemic), powers undefined, no preparedness framework, no compensation; New PH Bill — comprehensive, rights-based, surveillance, one-health approach
India में Epidemic Diseases Act को 2015 में replace किया गया
New Public Health Law — unnecessary है

explanation: Epidemic Diseases Act 1897 — limitations: (1) Only 4 sections, colonial era, (2) No definition of 'epidemic,' (3) State powers only (section 2), (4) No preparedness or surveillance framework, (5) No rights protection, (6) No compensation for affected, (7) No health emergency standards. COVID revealed gaps → DM Act 2005 invoked. Proposed Public Health (Prevention, Control and Management of Epidemics, Bio-terrorism and Disasters) Bill — comprehensive, (2017 draft) pending। Features: One Health, rights-based, compensations, surveillance system।

question: भारत में 'Drugs and Cosmetics Act 1940' के तहत 'Schedule H1' और 'Schedule X' का स्वास्थ्य नीति में क्या महत्व है?

options.text: ये schedules — cosmetics के लिए हैं
H1 — prescription-only drugs (antibiotics, steroids); Schedule X — psychotropic substances requiring special prescription and records — misuse prevention
Schedule H1 — OTC drugs हैं
Drugs Act 1940 — केवल manufacturing को regulate करता है

explanation: Drugs and Cosmetics Act 1940: Schedule H1 (2014 amendment) — high-risk drugs (3rd generation antibiotics, anti-TB, anti-retroviral) — licensed pharmacist, prescription mandatory, pharmacy records kept 3 years. Schedule X — psychotropics, narcotics (morphine, tramadol) — special prescription pad, double records. Significance: (1) Antibiotic stewardship, (2) Prevent drug misuse/addiction, (3) TB — DOTS compliance, (4) Opioid access for palliative care — difficult due to Schedule X complexity (Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act 1985 also applies)।

question: भारत में 'National Commission for Backward Classes' (NCBC) और OBC health provisions में क्या संबंध है?

options.text: NCBC — केवल education reservations देखता है
102वें संशोधन द्वारा NCBC — constitutional body बना; OBC inclusion → Mandal quotas in medical education; OBC health workers → community reach, service equity
NCBC — health से completely unrelated
NCBC — state list का विषय है

explanation: 102nd Constitutional Amendment (2018) — NCBC → Article 338-B (constitutional body). OBC reservation (27%) in Central services + medical colleges (post-Mandal). Health implications: (1) OBC reservation in MBBS, PG medical seats → more OBC doctors, (2) OBC health workers → cultural proximity with communities, (3) OBC anganwadi workers, ASHA in OBC villages → better service uptake, (4) OBC community health insurance — PM-JAY coverage. EWS 10% reservation (103rd Amendment) → economically weak patients also covered।

question: भारत में 'Biological Diversity Act 2002' और स्वास्थ्य के पारंपरिक ज्ञान (Traditional Knowledge) संरक्षण में इसकी क्या भूमिका है?

options.text: Biological Diversity Act — केवल wildlife protection के लिए
BD Act — ABS (Access and Benefit Sharing) framework; Traditional Knowledge of tribal healers protected; bio-piracy prevention; National Biodiversity Authority oversees
Traditional Knowledge — BD Act में covered नहीं
BD Act — Intellectual Property Rights Act का part है

explanation: Biological Diversity Act 2002: Implements CBD (Convention on Biological Diversity). Three tiers: National Biodiversity Authority (NBA), State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs), Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs) at local level. Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) — Nagoya Protocol aligned. Traditional Knowledge (TK): (1) Documentation — Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL) — 35 million pages, (2) Prior Informed Consent required for foreign access, (3) Benefit sharing with local communities/healers. Anti-bio-piracy: neem, turmeric patents challenged using TKDL। Community Health — traditional medicine practitioners' rights।

question: भारत में 'Tobacco Control' नीति में केंद्र और राज्य की क्या भूमिकाएँ हैं?

options.text: Tobacco control — केवल state का विषय है
COTPA 2003 — Central legislation; states — enforcement, penalties enhancement, graphic health warnings, public places ban; India के WHO FCTC obligations
Tobacco — Union List का विषय है, states को कोई role नहीं
India में tobacco control law 2017 में बना

explanation: COTPA (Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act 2003): Central law. Provisions: (1) Cigarette pack warnings (85% graphic health warning), (2) Smoking bans in public places, (3) No sale near educational institutions (100 meters), (4) No advertising. State role: (1) Enforcement through police/magistrates, (2) Can be stricter, (3) Penalty provisions. WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (FCTC) 2003 — India signatory. ITC taxes — Ministry of Finance. NTCP (National Tobacco Control Programme) — NHM component। SUA (Smoke-free areas) compliance।

question: भारत में 'National Commission for Protection of Child Rights' (NCPCR) और 'Juvenile Justice Act 2015' का health context में क्या महत्व है?

options.text: JJ Act — केवल criminal juvenile matters के लिए
JJ Act 2015 — Child Care Institutions में healthcare mandatory; NCPCR — nutrition, vaccination, mental health of institutionalized children monitor करती है; POCSO — health evidence protocols
JJ Act 2015 — health से असंबंधित
NCPCR — जेलों में बच्चों को देखती है

explanation: JJ (Care and Protection of Children) Act 2015: Sections on health in Child Care Institutions: (1) Medical examination within 24 hours of admission, (2) Regular health check-ups, (3) Mental health services, (4) Medical treatment records. NCPCR mandate: (1) Monitor nutrition status in CCIs, (2) Vaccination coverage in children's homes, (3) Mental health of children in conflict with law, (4) POCSO — child-friendly medical examination protocols. 'Bal Swaraj' portal — NCPCR online monitoring of CCIs। Child trafficking → health consequences also monitored।

question: भारत में 'National Food Security Act 2013' के 'Grievance Redressal Mechanism' का क्या प्रावधान है?

options.text: NFSA में कोई grievance mechanism नहीं
District Grievance Redressal Officer (DGRO), State Food Commission, third-party audit — NFSA की accountability chain
केवल RTI से शिकायत की जा सकती है
NFSA grievances — High Court में ही जाती हैं

explanation: NFSA 2013 — Grievance Redressal: (1) District Grievance Redressal Officer (DGRO) — entitlement-related complaints, (2) State Food Commission — DGRO orders on appeal, central oversight, (3) Third-party evaluation of scheme, (4) Social audit by Gram Sabha (rural areas). Health connection: NFSA PDS → nutrition → health. Grievance when PDS grain denied → nutrition affected → child health. PDS + ICDS + MDM convergence — all have grievance systems. Food courts — some states established।

question: भारत में 'Inter-State River Water Disputes Act 1956' और स्वास्थ्य में water-health nexus का क्या महत्व है?

options.text: River water disputes — health से असंबंधित
Water allocation conflicts → downstream communities का drinking water availability → waterborne disease burden; Cauvery, Krishna, Godavari disputes → affected communities' health
River water disputes — केवल agricultural interest
IS River Water Disputes — अनुच्छेद 131 से ही सुलझाए जाते हैं

explanation: Inter-State Water Disputes Act 1956 (Art. 262): Tribunals for Cauvery (Karnataka-TN), Krishna, Godavari, Mahanadi, etc. Health implications: (1) Reduced water flow → drinking water scarcity → communities revert to unsafe sources → waterborne disease, (2) Riparian communities — arsenic/fluoride contamination disputes, (3) Dam-affected communities — displacement → healthcare disruption, (4) Irrigation conflicts → agricultural communities' food security → nutrition. Water as SDH — water governance = health governance।

question: भारत में '12वीं पंचवर्षीय योजना' (2012-17) और उसके बाद 'NITI Aayog Vision 2035' में स्वास्थ्य की प्राथमिकताएँ क्या थीं?

options.text: 12th Plan में health — secondary priority
12th Plan: Universal Health Coverage, mental health, NCD focus, RMNCH+A; NITI Vision 2035: Preventive Health, Universal Health Coverage, health technology — progressive evolution
NITI Aayog — no health vision document
12th Plan और NITI Vision — identical health priorities

explanation: 12th Five Year Plan (2012-17): (1) Universal Health Coverage (UHC) — Shri B K Chaturvedi Committee, (2) RMNCH+A (Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child and Adolescent Health), (3) NCD National Programme, (4) Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana expansion, (5) Mental health focus. NITI Aayog Health Vision 2035 (2019): (1) Digital health, (2) Preventive health focus, (3) UHC through PMJAY + CPHC, (4) Health technology innovation, (5) Disease surveillance modernization। Planning Commission → NITI Aayog shift: indicative to aspirational planning।

question: भारत में 'Consumer Protection in Healthcare' के संदर्भ में 'Medical Negligence' के निर्धारण में कौन-से कानूनी मानक हैं?

options.text: Medical Negligence — किसी भी गलत treatment में
Bolam Test (reasonable doctor standard) + Jacob Mathew Case 2005 (SC India) — negligence ≠ mere error; gross negligence या recklessness required — IPC 304A + Consumer Protection
India में Medical Negligence — no law
Medical Negligence — only criminal law applicable

explanation: Medical Negligence legal standards in India: (1) Bolam Test (UK 1957): Doctor not negligent if acted per accepted medical practice (supported by reputable body of doctors), (2) Jacob Mathew v. State of Punjab (SC 2005): For criminal negligence — must show gross, reckless, lack of reasonable care; mere error not criminal. (3) IPC 304A — negligent act causing death, (4) Consumer Protection Act — Medical service = 'service'; negligence → compensation, (5) Civil suits for damages. Health Education: Medical practitioners' rights + accountability balance।

question: भारत में 'Right to Health Bill' (Draft 2021) और इसकी आवश्यकता का विश्लेषण करें।

options.text: India में Right to Health already a Fundamental Right है
Art. 21 से derived, पर justiciable statutory right absent; Draft Bill — उचित health care का कानूनी अधिकार, mandatory primary care, no denial of emergency treatment, accountability framework
Rajasthan Right to Health Act 2023 — first in India, paved way for central bill
Right to Health Bill — Parliament में पास हो गया

explanation: Right to Health in India: Currently implied under Art. 21 (paschim Banga case). Not explicitly justiciable statutory right. Rajasthan Right to Health Act 2023 — India's first state law: (1) Free outpatient services at public hospitals, (2) Emergency care rights (no denial even if no money), (3) Patient rights charter, (4) Grievance mechanism. Doctors' strike against — controversy. Draft National Right to Health Bill: (1) Universal right to quality healthcare, (2) Emergency care free, (3) Health ombudsman, (4) Patient rights. UHC target alignment।

question: भारत में 'Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes' के लिए 'Special Component Plan' और 'Tribal Sub-Plan' का health budgeting में क्या महत्व है?

options.text: दोनों plans अब बंद हो गए हैं
SC Sub-Plan और TSP — SC/ST जनसंख्या अनुपात में health budget allocate करना — earmarked funds — proper implementation poor
SC/ST Sub-Plans — केवल education sector में
Tribal Sub-Plan — Ministry of Tribal Affairs का कार्यक्रम है केवल

explanation: SC Sub-Plan (now SCSP) and Tribal Sub-Plan (TSP) — 5th FYP से: SC और ST population के अनुपात में सभी departments के budget में earmarking। MHFW SCSP/TSP: health funds specifically for SC/ST communities। Challenges: (1) Merged with general budget (some states), (2) Poor tracking, (3) Funds diverted, (4) Implementation at ground level weak. Positive: Forces data disaggregation for SC/ST health outcomes. State-specific TSP: Odisha, Chhattisgarh tribal health allocations। Adivasi health equity।

question: भारत में 'National Rural Health Mission' (2005) के लागू होने से पहले की ग्रामीण स्वास्थ्य अवसंरचना की स्थिति क्या थी?

options.text: NRHM से पहले India में primary health care excellent था
Pre-NRHM: severe infrastructure gap (Bhore Report gap still existing), staff vacancies, supply chain failures, no community health workers, poor accountability — NRHM जवाब था
NRHM — already working primary care को और बेहतर बनाया
NRHM से पहले कोई rural health structure नहीं था

explanation: Pre-NRHM situation (pre-2005): (1) PHC/CHC shortfall — 40% PHCs closed half day, (2) Doctor vacancies — 70% rural posts vacant, (3) Essential drugs unavailable at public facilities, (4) No formal CHW — ASHA not existed, (5) Institutional deliveries — only 40% nationally, (6) High MMR (301/lakh LB) and IMR (58/1000 LB), (7) Poor accountability. NRHM (2005) — Community Processes (ASHA), Untied Funds (Rs 10,000/sub-center), IPHS norms, RKS, DLHS tracking, state flexibility। Paradigm shift।

question: भारत में 'Central Government Health Scheme' (CGHS) और 'Employee State Insurance' (ESI) में क्या अंतर है?

options.text: दोनों एक ही हैं
CGHS — Central govt employees + pensioners (tax-funded); ESI — organized sector workers (contributory, payroll deduction) — अलग beneficiary groups, different financing
ESI — only accident insurance
CGHS — private sector employees को cover करता है

explanation: CGHS (Central Government Health Scheme) — 1954: (1) Central govt employees + pensioners + dependents, (2) Tax-funded (employer = Central Govt), (3) CGHS wellness centers across cities, (4) Cashless in empanelled hospitals, (5) Drug supply from CGHS pharmacies. ESI (Employees' State Insurance) — ESIC (1948): (1) Organized sector employees (income ≤ ₹21,000/month), (2) Contributory: Employee 0.75% + Employer 3.25% of wages, (3) ESI dispensaries + hospitals, (4) Comprehensive: medical, sickness benefit, maternity, disability. Both cover only formal sector।

question: भारत में 'Public Private Partnership' (PPP) स्वास्थ्य में किन प्रमुख models में है?

options.text: PPP health में नहीं होती
Concession (BOT), Management Contract, Social Franchise (Jan Aushadhi), Contracting-in (specialists), Output-based Aid (Janani Express) — multiple PPP models
PPP — केवल hospital building में
PPP — India में constitutionally prohibited

explanation: PPP Health Models in India: (1) Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) — private builds, operates, transfers (e.g., Rajasthan DISHA PPP), (2) Management Contract — private manages public facility, (3) Social Franchise — standardized quality private clinics (accredited social health franchises), (4) Jan Aushadhi — government generic drug retail through private franchisees, (5) Contracting-in — private specialists in PHC/CHC, (6) PPP diagnostics — free diagnostics in public hospitals (UP, Delhi), (7) Ambulance services — 108/102 by private operators. NHM PPP guidelines. PPP risks: cherry-picking, quality assurance challenges।

question: भारत में 'स्वास्थ्य और परिवार कल्याण मंत्रालय' के अंतर्गत कौन-से प्रमुख विभाग हैं?

options.text: केवल एक विभाग
Department of Health & Family Welfare और Department of Health Research (ICMR के अंतर्गत) — दोनों
तीन विभाग: Health, Family Welfare, AYUSH
AYUSH — MoHFW का हिस्सा है

explanation: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW): (1) Department of Health and Family Welfare — NHM, Hospital Services, Drug Regulation (CDSCO), Blood Safety, Mental Health, (2) Department of Health Research — ICMR (Indian Council of Medical Research), biomedical research funding. Note: Ministry of AYUSH — separate ministry (since 2014). Pharmaceutical Department — Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers। National Health Mission — under DoHFW। Health education — HEO cadre under state DoHFW।

question: भारत में 'Lokur Committee 1970' (Scheduled Tribes criteria) और health equity में इसकी क्या relevance है?

options.text: Lokur Committee — education के बारे में थी
Lokur Committee ने ST definition के 5 criteria दिए — सही identification → constitutional safeguards → health schemes eligibility; wrong ST listing → health deprivation
Lokur Committee recommendations — कभी accepted नहीं हुई
ST criteria — केवल economic poverty based हैं

explanation: Lokur Committee (1965, report 1970) — Criteria for ST: (1) Tribal origin and primitive traits, (2) Geographical isolation, (3) Shyness of contact with community at large, (4) Backwardness in general, (5) Distinct culture. Health relevance: (1) Correct ST listing → PVTG scheme eligibility (special health schemes), (2) Tribal Sub-Plan health components, (3) FRA rights → medicinal plants, (4) 6th Schedule health provisions, (5) Tribal health program targeting. Fraudulent ST claims → real tribes deprived। NHRC monitoring।

question: भारत में 'Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana' (RSBY 2008) के अनुभव से PM-JAY 2018 ने क्या सीखा?

options.text: PM-JAY और RSBY — identical schemes हैं
RSBY — ₹30,000 limit inadequate; enrollment quality poor; asymmetric information problems; PM-JAY — ₹5 lakh, cashless, secondary/tertiary focus, technology-driven, convergent
RSBY — successful था, PM-JAY unnecessary था
RSBY — केवल अस्पताल निर्माण था

explanation: RSBY (2008) — ₹30,000/family/year for BPL families, 5 members, smart card system. Lessons: (1) Low limit → catastrophic expenditure still occurred, (2) Enrollment errors — non-poor included, poor excluded, (3) Adverse selection, (4) Provider fraud (unnecessary procedures), (5) Limited secondary care coverage, (6) State variation. PM-JAY improvements: (1) ₹5 lakh limit (10x higher), (2) SECC-based identification (better targeting), (3) Technology — QR code, Aadhaar verification, (4) Cashless secondary + tertiary, (5) Expanded to 1,929 procedures, (6) Portability across India।

question: भारत में 'Swachh Bharat Mission' (SBM) के health co-benefits को political science के 'intersectoral policy' दृष्टिकोण से समझाएँ।

options.text: SBM — केवल sanitation program है, health से unrelated
SBM — ODF achievement → reduced diarrheal disease, child stunting, IMR; women's safety and dignity; school attendance — intersectoral health dividend through political will
SBM का health impact — सिद्ध नहीं हुआ
SBM — health ministry का program है

explanation: Swachh Bharat Mission (2014): Phase I (rural + urban, 2014-19) — ODF (Open Defecation Free) achievement by Oct 2, 2019 (claimed). Phase 2 (2020-24+) — solid waste management, ODF++, faecal sludge management. Health co-benefits evidence: (1) Diarrheal disease 45% reduction (UNICEF modelling), (2) Under-5 stunting reduction — 5.7% reduction linked (Bill & Melinda Gates study), (3) Women's safety — no open defecation at night → fewer sexual assaults, (4) School girls' retention — separate toilets. Political dimensions: High PM priority → fast implementation → governance demonstrates intersectoral health।

question: भारत में 'PM Poshan' (Mid-Day Meal Scheme renamed) और 'Right to Education Act 2009' का स्वास्थ्य-शिक्षा nexus क्या है?

options.text: Mid-Day Meal — केवल food scheme है
MDM → school enrollment + retention + nutrition → child health improvement; RTE — 6-14 years education guarantee → health literacy platform
RTE — health से असंबंधित
Mid-Day Meal — private schools में compulsory नहीं है

explanation: PM Poshan (formerly MDM Scheme, 1995) — Supreme Court Order 2001 (PUCL v. Union) mandated it. Health benefits: (1) 10+ crore children served daily, (2) Reduced class-room hunger → attention, learning, (3) Micronutrient supplementation (iron, folic acid, vitamin A in meal), (4) Deworming, (5) Enrollment especially of girls. RTE (2009) — Free and Compulsory Education 6-14 years → school as health platform (screening, vaccination, health education). School Health Programme (NHM + RTE) — linkage। Adolescent health education in schools → reproductive health।

question: भारत में 'National Policy on AYUSH' (Ayurveda, Yoga, Unani, Siddha, Homeopathy) के mainstreaming में क्या political और institutional challenges हैं?

options.text: AYUSH — केवल cultural heritage है, clinical value नहीं
AYUSH Ministry (2014) — अलग identity; mainstreaming challenges: evidence gap, integration with allopathy (turf conflicts), regulation standardization, drug quality, practitioner competency
AYUSH — fully evidence-based और integrated
AYUSH — WHO द्वारा endorsed नहीं है

explanation: Ministry of AYUSH (2014, separate from MoHFW): Ayurveda, Yoga, Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, Homeopathy. Challenges: (1) Evidence — RCT evidence limited for most therapies, (2) Turf conflict — IMA vs AYUSH practitioners, (3) Drug quality — 34% AYUSH drugs fail quality test (CAG 2023), (4) Regulation — Ayurveda drugs regulated under D&C Act Schedule E (inadequate), (5) COVID — CORONIL controversy — evidence vs claim. Opportunities: (1) HWC Yoga program, (2) AYUSH HWC integration, (3) WHO Traditional Medicine Strategy. NHP 2017 — integration envisaged।

question: भारत में 'National AIDS Control Organization' (NACO) की governance structure और 'NACP IV' की मुख्य रणनीतियाँ क्या हैं?

options.text: NACO — WHO का India chapter है
NACO — MoHFW autonomous body; NACP IV (2012-17) — zero new infections, zero AIDS-related deaths, zero stigma; NACP V — treatment expansion, PrEP, key population focus
NACO — केवल awareness campaigns
NACP IV — पूरी तरह सफल रहा, new HIV cases — zero

explanation: NACO: (1) Autonomous body under MoHFW, (2) National AIDS and STD Control Programme, (3) State AIDS Control Societies (SACS) — state level, (4) District AIDS Prevention and Control Units (DAPCUs). NACP IV goals: zero new HIV infections, zero AIDS-related deaths, zero discrimination. Strategies: (1) Key population focus (sex workers, IDU, MSM, transgender), (2) Prevention of Parent to Child Transmission (PPTCT), (3) Free ART (Antiretroviral Treatment), (4) TI (Targeted Interventions), (5) Blood safety. India — AIDS response globally praised. HIV Act 2017 — legal protection for PLHIV।

question: भारत में 'प्रधानमंत्री राष्ट्रीय राहत कोष' (PMNRF) और 'आरोग्य निधि' का health welfare में क्या उपयोग है?

options.text: PMNRF — political fund है
PMNRF — disaster relief + major surgery financial assistance to poor patients; Arogya Nidhi — BPL patients में Rs. 1.5 lakh तक medical assistance — आर्थिक कठिनाई में
PMNRF — केवल natural disasters के लिए
Arogya Nidhi — PM-JAY का हिस्सा है

explanation: PMNRF (Prime Minister's National Relief Fund): (1) Public contributions, (2) Major life-threatening illness treatment assistance, (3) Medical treatment for organs (transplant) — BPL patients. Arogya Nidhi: (1) National Illness Assistance Fund → States → State Illness Assistance Funds (SIAF), (2) BPL patients, (3) Life-threatening conditions, (4) Rs. 1.5 lakh for specified conditions, (5) Not covered by other insurance. Health welfare funds complement PM-JAY for conditions outside its scope. Cancer treatment, heart surgery, kidney transplant — PMNRF/Arogya Nidhi supported।

question: भारत में 'Indian Public Health Standards' (IPHS) क्या निर्धारित करती है और इसकी compliance की क्या स्थिति है?

options.text: IPHS — केवल private hospitals के लिए
IPHS — Sub-Centre, PHC, CHC, SDH, District Hospital के लिए infrastructure, human resources, equipment, service standards — compliance अभी भी 50-60% है
IPHS — केवल HR standards
IPHS compliance — 100% है

explanation: IPHS (Indian Public Health Standards) — NHM 2007 (revised 2012): (1) Infrastructure: SC (2 rooms + toilet), PHC (6-bed), CHC (30-bed), SDH (100-bed), DH (varies), (2) Human resources: PHC = 1 MBBS + 1 LHV + 2 ANMs + 1 pharmacist, (3) Essential drugs + equipment, (4) Service delivery norms, (5) Quality accreditation (NQAS). Compliance status (DLHS-4, RHS 2022): (1) ~30% PHCs function 24×7, (2) Significant drug stock-outs, (3) Doctor shortages. NQA (National Quality Assurance) — Kayakalp award for clean hospitals।

question: भारत में 'Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health' के क्या कार्य हैं और इसने हाल के वर्षों में किन health issues को उठाया है?

options.text: Health Standing Committee — केवल budget review करती है
Bills scrutiny, demand for grants examination, policy review, ministry accountability — heatwave deaths, antibiotic resistance, generic drugs, NHM funding gaps उठाए
Parliamentary Health Committee — केवल doctors द्वारा composed है
Health Committee — राज्यसभा में नहीं होती

explanation: Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare: (1) Members from both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, (2) Examines bills (NMC Bill, Drugs Act Amendment), (3) Scrutinizes Demands for Grants (Health Budget), (4) Ministry accountability. Recent reports: (1) Drug pricing — NPPA effectiveness, (2) Generic medicine availability (Jan Aushadhi), (3) NHM funding shortfalls, (4) Medical education quality (NMC), (5) Antibiotic resistance policy, (6) COVID pandemic preparedness gaps, (7) Mental health system gaps. Important oversight body। Committee reports tabled in Parliament।

question: भारत में 'National Medical Commission Act 2020' (NMC) ने 'Medical Council of India' (MCI) को replace क्यों किया?

options.text: MCI — perfectly functional था, NMC necessary नहीं था
MCI corruption scandals (capitation fees, college recognition), regulatory failure → NMC: 33-member commission, autonomous boards, NEXT exam, community health training
NMC — केवल cosmetic change है
MCI — 1950 में बना था, outdated

explanation: MCI (Medical Council of India, 1934 Act) — problems: (1) Corruption — Ketan Desai case (arrested 2010), (2) Medical college recognition irregularities, (3) Capitation fee racket, (4) Poor enforcement of curriculum quality, (5) Self-regulated (doctors regulating doctors). NMC Act 2020: (1) 33-member National Medical Commission, (2) 4 autonomous boards (UG, PG, assessment, ethics), (3) NEXT (National Exit Test) — single licensing exam, (4) Community health doctor provisions, (5) Autonomy to colleges, (6) Ethics Board more independent. Controversies: capitation fees (section 10D), bridge course।

question: भारत में 'One Health' approach और सरकारी नीतियों में इसकी पहचान कहाँ होती है?

options.text: One Health — India में अपरिचित concept है
Human-Animal-Environment interface; zoonotic diseases (COVID, Nipah, avian flu); National One Health Mission — intersectoral coordination; ICMR-NIV-ICAR-MoEF collaboration
One Health — केवल veterinary medicine है
India में One Health के लिए कोई governance mechanism नहीं

explanation: One Health — WHO/FAO/OIE concept: human, animal, environmental health interconnected. India's response: (1) National One Health Mission (PM-ABHIM component) — zoonotic disease surveillance, (2) Nipah (Kerala) — human+bat+pig interface, (3) COVID — possible animal origin, (4) Antimicrobial Resistance — agriculture overuse of antibiotics. Governance: (1) National Expert Group on One Health (2021), (2) MoHFW + Ministry of Animal Husbandry + MoEF coordination, (3) ICMR — research, (4) NCDC — surveillance. Global: WHO-World Bank One Health Joint Plan।

question: भारत में 'Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana' (PMSSY) का क्या उद्देश्य है और इसके अंतर्गत कौन-से संस्थान हैं?

options.text: PMSSY — health insurance scheme है
AIIMS (6 new initially, now 22+) और Government Medical Colleges upgradation — tertiary care और health education quality improvement — underserved states में
PMSSY — केवल Delhi AIIMS के लिए
PMSSY — private hospital construction के लिए subsidy

explanation: PMSSY (Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana, 2006): Two components: (1) New AIIMS — 6 initially (Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Jodhpur, Patna, Raipur, Rishikesh) → expanded to 22+ across India, (2) Upgradation of existing Government Medical Colleges. Objectives: (1) Address regional imbalance in tertiary healthcare, (2) Reduce medical tourism within India, (3) Train more doctors for rural areas, (4) Research capacity. New AIIMS fully functional — Mangalagiri, Bibinagar, Gorakhpur, Kalyani, etc. Significant investment in healthcare infrastructure।

question: भारत में 'National Health Mission' के 'Flexible Pool' और 'Rigid Pool' funding का क्या अर्थ है?

options.text: दोनों एक ही हैं
Flexible Pool — states अपनी priorities के अनुसार use कर सकते हैं (State Specific Needs); Rigid Pool — central priorities के लिए (Immunization, FP, RMNCH) — fixed allocations
Flexible Pool — केवल NE states के लिए
NHM में कोई flexible funding नहीं है

explanation: NHM Flexible Financing: (1) Rigid Pool/Central Pool — core programs: immunization, family planning, TB, malaria, leprosy, blindness — centrally designed and funded, (2) Flexible Pool — state specific: block-level planning (DHAP), state innovations, state-specific disease burden. State gets Flexible Pool based on PIP (Program Implementation Plan) approval. Benefits: (1) Addresses local epidemiology, (2) State innovation (Tamil Nadu maternal health model), (3) Accountability through PIPs. Challenges: PIP approval delays, unspent funds lapse। Finance: Centre 60:State 40।

question: भारत में 'Compulsory Licensing' (CL) pharmaceutical drugs में क्या है और Natco-Bayer case का क्या महत्व है?

options.text: Compulsory Licensing — drug manufacturing ban है
TRIPS Article 31 के तहत public health में government third party को patent drug बनाने का license दे सकती है — India ने पहली CL 2012 में Bayer's Sorafenib के लिए Natco को दी
CL — India में कभी issue नहीं हुआ
CL — only for vaccines

explanation: Compulsory License (Patents Act 1970, Section 84): Government can license third party to make patented drug without patent holder's consent — conditions: not reasonably available, not at reasonable price, or not worked in India. India's CL: March 2012 — Controller General of Patents issued CL to Natco Pharma for Bayer's Sorafenib (Nexavar — liver/kidney cancer) — Natco could sell at ₹8,800/month vs ₹2.8 lakh. Doha Declaration (2001) — public health over patents. India's Patents Act Section 3(d) — prevents evergreening (Novartis Gleevec case 2013)। Access to medicines — political economy।

question: भारत में 'Niti Aayog State Health Index' और इसके मुख्य indicators का विश्लेषण करें।

options.text: NITI Aayog Health Index — only economic indicators
Health Outcomes (NMR, U5MR, institutional delivery, full immunization) + Governance and Processes + Key Inputs/Processes — 3 domain index; Kerala consistently tops
State Health Index — केवल total spending measure करता है
Health Index — केवल 10 states के लिए

explanation: NITI Aayog Health Index (since 2017, annual): 3 domains: (1) Health Outcomes — NMR (Neonatal Mortality Rate), U5MR, MMR, full immunization, institutional delivery (70% weight), (2) Governance & Information (10%) — HMIS quality, financial management, (3) Key Inputs/Processes (20%) — ANM vacancy, doctors, beds, drugs. Categories: Large states, Small states, UTs. Consistently top: Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Telangana (large states). Improved most: Rajasthan, HP, J&K. Used for: Centre-State performance-based incentives (reward good performers)।

question: भारत में 'Menstrual Hygiene Management' (MHM) policy में केंद्र और राज्य सरकारों के क्या प्रयास हैं?

options.text: MHM — government policy में नहीं
National MHM Guidelines (2015), Swachh Bharat-school toilets, sanitary napkin subsidies (Suvidha scheme, Saathi), free napkins in ASHA kits, school health curriculum — multi-ministry
MHM — केवल NGO कार्य है
India में free sanitary napkins — all women को provide किए जाते हैं

explanation: MHM in India: (1) National MHM Guidelines 2015 — policy framework, (2) Swachh Bharat Mission — separate girls' toilets in schools with incinerator/disposal, (3) 'Suvidha' brand — subsidized sanitary napkins through ASHA (₹1/pad), (4) 'Saathi' program — school girls (MHRD), (5) ASHA kit — free pads to promote institutional delivery (Janani Suraksha incentive), (6) GST reduction on sanitary pads (2018 — 12% to 0%), (7) School Health Programme curriculum — menstrual health education. Adolescent health strategy — RKSK।

question: भारत में 'Clinical Establishments Act 2010' का क्या महत्व है और राज्यों में इसकी क्या स्थिति है?

options.text: All India Act है और सभी राज्यों में लागू है
All hospitals/clinics के registration + minimum standards — voluntary adoption by states; कई बड़े states ने adopt नहीं किया — regulatory gap
Clinical Establishments Act — केवल private hospitals के लिए
Act — 2020 में replaced हुआ

explanation: Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act 2010: Initially applicable to states consenting under Article 252. Provisions: (1) Registration mandatory for all clinical establishments, (2) Minimum standards (infrastructure, services), (3) Display of rates (services/procedures), (4) Maintaining records. Adopted by: Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Sikkim, UTs, J&K. NOT adopted: Maharashtra, Karnataka, Kerala, TN, West Bengal (have own laws). Gap: Major private hospital hubs without central regulation. Consumer Protection Act + CPA as default recourse।

question: भारत की 'National Population Policy 2000' (NPP 2000) के तीन स्तरीय जनसंख्या लक्ष्य और उनकी नीतिगत विशेषताएं क्या हैं?

options.text: NPP 2000 — केवल परिवार नियोजन तक सीमित
Immediate goal: unmet contraceptive need पूरा; Medium-term: TFR 2.1 by 2010; Long-term: 2045 तक stable population — rights-based, target-free approach + ICPD Cairo framework
NPP 2000 — compulsory sterilization की नीति है
TFR लक्ष्य — केवल UP-Bihar के लिए

explanation: National Population Policy 2000 (NPP 2000): Immediate goals: (1) Reduce MMR <100/lakh LB, (2) Reduce IMR <30/1000 LB, (3) Universal immunization, (4) 80% institutional delivery. Medium-term: TFR 2.1 by 2010 (not achieved — India reached 2.0 only ~2020). Long-term: stable population by 2045. Key principles: (1) Target-free approach (no sterilization quotas), (2) Rights-based — informed choice, (3) ICPD Cairo 1994 framework — reproductive rights. Mission Parivar Vikas (2016) for High Focus districts (UP, Bihar, MP, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Assam) — 146 high TFR districts।

question: 'Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)' के governance mechanism और इसकी accountability structure में क्या प्रमुख विशेषताएं हैं?

options.text: JSY — Centrally Sponsored Scheme नहीं है
JSY (2005) — 100% CSS, conditional cash transfer (Low Performing States में अधिक), ASHA linkage, district + state के माध्यम से fund flow, beneficiary-level accountability
JSY — केवल urban areas में
JSY — State government की पूर्ण funded scheme है

explanation: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) governance: (1) 100% Centrally Sponsored Scheme — no state share, (2) Cash transfer: LPS (Low Performing States) — ₹1400 rural, ₹1000 urban; HPS ₹700/600, (3) Beneficiary: BPL/SC/ST/below 19 age (originally). (4) ASHA role: registers pregnant women, accompanies to facility, gets incentive (₹600 rural LPS), (5) Fund flow: NHM state treasury → district health society → PHC → ASHA/beneficiary, (6) Accountability: MCP card, beneficiary register, ASHA diary, HMIS reporting, (7) Evaluation: NFHS data shows institutional delivery improvement (from 39% 2005 to 89% 2021)।

question: भारत में ASHA की 'legal status' और 'labour rights' को लेकर क्या प्रमुख विवाद और नीतिगत प्रश्न हैं?

options.text: ASHA — government employee हैं और ESI/PF मिलता है
ASHA — 'volunteer' या 'incentive-based worker' — permanent employee नहीं; न minimum wage, न ESI/PF; ASHA strikes ने regular pay और social protection की मांग की
ASHA को ₹15,000/month fixed salary मिलती है
ASHA — state government employees की तरह pension eligible हैं

explanation: ASHA labour rights controversy: (1) Official status: 'Accredited Social Health Activist' — volunteer/community health worker, not employee, (2) Remuneration: performance-based incentives (not salary) — varies ₹1500-6000/month depending on activities and state top-up, (3) No ESI, PF, pension, maternity leave, (4) ASHA Strikes (multiple 2017-2023): demanded ₹18,000/month + employee status, (5) Government position: ASHAs are 'volunteers' — converting to employees would change program design, (6) SC ruling (2021): acknowledged ASHA contributions but didn't grant employee status, (7) States like Kerala provide better packages. HEO must understand this structural inequity।

question: WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (FCTC) के तहत भारत की क्या अंतर्राष्ट्रीय प्रतिबद्धताएं हैं और COTPA 2003 कैसे उन्हें implement करता है?

options.text: India ने FCTC ratify नहीं किया है
India ने FCTC 2004 में ratify किया; COTPA 2003 — FCTC Articles implement करता है: Article 8 (smoke-free places), Article 11 (warnings), Article 13 (advertising ban), Article 14 (cessation)
FCTC — केवल WHO member countries पर binding है, India पर नहीं
COTPA 2003 — FCTC के पहले बना, इसलिए FCTC relevant नहीं

explanation: India & FCTC: (1) India ratified FCTC in 2004 (one of first), (2) COTPA 2003 (Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act) — key provisions: Section 4 — smoke-free public places, Section 5 — advertising/promotion ban, Section 6 — no sale near educational institutions, pictorial warnings (85% packaging — among world's largest), (3) FCTC compliance gaps: no illicit trade protocol implementation, smokeless tobacco regulation weak, (4) National Tobacco Control Programme (NTCP) — district-level IEC, cessation, (5) Challenge: India — world's 2nd largest tobacco consumer; 1.3 million deaths/year, (6) MPOWER: Monitor, Protect, Offer cessation, Warn, Enforce bans, Raise taxes।

question: 'Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act 2016' (RPWD Act) में health से संबंधित क्या प्रावधान हैं और HEO की क्या भूमिका है?

options.text: RPWD Act 2016 — health provisions नहीं हैं
RPWD Act 2016: 21 disability categories, health insurance समानता, free health care BPL PWDs, rehabilitation, accessible health facilities, disability certificate — CMO द्वारा
RPWD Act — PWD Act 1995 के समान है
RPWD Act — केवल education और employment के लिए है

explanation: RPWD Act 2016 health provisions: (1) 21 disability categories (vs 7 in PWD 1995) including mental illness, autism, intellectual disability, (2) Section 25: equal health care, no discrimination; accessible healthcare facilities, (3) Section 26: free health services (BPL PWDs) — government hospitals, (4) Section 27: manpower development — disability-inclusive health education, (5) Insurance: no discrimination (Section 25(3)), (6) Disability Certificate: CMO/Chief Medical Officer issues — gate-keeper role for HEO, (7) DISHA programme under Ministry of Social Justice (early intervention), (8) Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat) — health facility accessibility. HEO: ensures PWD-friendly PHC, disability data in HMIS।

question: भारत की 'National Mental Health Policy 2014' और 'Mental Healthcare Act 2017' में राज्य की जिम्मेदारियां क्या हैं?

options.text: Mental health — exclusively Central government responsibility है

NMHP 2014: vision, goals, strategic directions; MHCA 2017: rights-based framework — State Mental Health Authority (SMHA), mental health establishments registration, right to treatment, advance directive, nominated representative
NMHP 2014 और MHCA 2017 — same document हैं
Mental Health — Concurrent List में नहीं

explanation: National Mental Health Policy 2014: Vision: 'mentally healthy India'; Goals: prevention, access, community care, rights, research. Strategic directions: (1) community-based MH services, (2) integration with PHC (District Mental Health Programme — DMHP), (3) intersectoral coordination. Mental Healthcare Act 2017: (1) State Mental Health Authority (SMHA) — registration, monitoring of mental health establishments, (2) Rights: free basic MH services (BPL), informed consent, no solitary confinement/chaining, (3) Advance Directive — patient's wishes when capacity lost, (4) Nominated Representative, (5) Central MHA — national oversight. HEO role: DMHP implementation, MH awareness, stigma reduction।

question: भारत में '12वीं Schedule' (74वें संशोधन) में शामिल 'urban health' functions क्या हैं और ULBs की वास्तविक स्थिति क्या है?

options.text: 12th Schedule में health functions नहीं हैं
12th Schedule (18 functions): public health, hospitals, primary health, sanitation, SWM, water supply — ULBs को assign; but most states ने actual devolution नहीं किया — fund/function/functionary gap
ULBs को 12th Schedule से full autonomy मिल गई है
Urban health — केवल Central government की जिम्मेदारी

explanation: 12th Schedule (74th Amendment, 1992): 18 functions listed for Urban Local Bodies including: (1) Public health, sanitation, conservancy, SWM, (2) Regulation of slaughterhouses, (3) Provision of urban amenities. Health-specific: hospitals, primary health, Mother and Child Care. Reality: (1) Only 8 functions effectively transferred on average (NIPFP study), (2) State governments retain control of major hospitals, (3) ULB health staff on deputation from state, (4) NUHM (National Urban Health Mission) — tried to fill gap, (5) Urban Health Resource Centres (UHRC) — SHC equivalent, (6) Smart Cities Mission — health facility upgrade in 100 cities. 3F devolution (Funds, Functions, Functionaries) — weak।

question: 'District Mineral Foundation (DMF)' और 'PMKKKY' का स्वास्थ्य क्षेत्र में क्या उपयोग है और इसका governance framework क्या है?

options.text: DMF — health activities के लिए use नहीं हो सकता
DMF (MMDR Act 2015) + PMKKKY: mining-affected districts में health infrastructure — PHC, hospitals, safe drinking water, sanitation; Governing Council में elected representatives + collector
DMF — केवल environment restoration के लिए है
DMF funds — State Consolidated Fund में जाते हैं

explanation: District Mineral Foundation (DMF): Created under MMDR (Amendment) Act 2015 — non-profit trust in mining districts. Funded by: miners paying % of royalty (major minerals 10-30%, minor minerals 10%). PMKKKY (Pradhan Mantri Khanij Kshetra Kalyan Yojana) — guidelines: 60% funds for priority works (drinking water, environment, health, education, livelihood); 40% for other development. Health uses: PHC building, equipment, ambulances, community health workers. Governance: DMF Trust with Collector/DM as ex-officio head, elected gram panchayat/municipality representatives. Total DMF collection: ₹50,000+ crore (2015-2023). Issues: slow utilization, lack of community participation।

question: भारत में 'National Nutrition Strategy 2017' और 'POSHAN Abhiyaan' के बीच क्या संबंध है और convergence का governance model क्या है?

options.text: National Nutrition Strategy 2017 और POSHAN Abhiyaan — असंबंधित हैं

National Nutrition Strategy 2017 (NITI Aayog) — policy framework; POSHAN Abhiyaan 2018 — implementation mechanism; Jan Andolan approach, technology-based monitoring (ICDS-CAS), convergence of 8+ departments
POSHAN Abhiyaan — केवल WCD Ministry का कार्यक्रम है
Stunting लक्ष्य 2022 तक 25% था — achieve हुआ

explanation: National Nutrition Strategy 2017 (NITI Aayog): Policy blueprint — reduce stunting, wasting, undernutrition, anemia. Key principle: nutrition-sensitive + nutrition-specific interventions. POSHAN Abhiyaan (PM's Overarching Scheme for Holistic Nourishment) 2018: (1) Targets: reduce stunting/wasting 2%/year, anemia 3%/year, LBW 2%/year, (2) Technology: ICDS-CAS (Common Application Software) for real-time monitoring, (3) Convergence: 8 ministries (WCD, Health, Drinking Water, Rural Dev, Tribal, Food, School Education, AYUSH), (4) Jan Andolan: community mobilization, (5) Poshan Maah (September), (6) Real-time data: growth monitoring through AWC. NFHS-5 (2019-21): stunting 35.5% (from 38.4%) — progress but goal not met।

question: भारत में 'Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) National Action Plan 2017' में स्वास्थ्य विभाग की क्या जिम्मेदारियां हैं?

options.text: AMR — केवल veterinary/agriculture problem है
India NAP on AMR 2017 (5 years): One Health approach — MoHFW, Animal Husbandry, Agriculture, Environment; surveillance (ICMR-AMR network), antibiotic stewardship, infection prevention, IEC, research
AMR — WHO की जिम्मेदारी है, India की नहीं
Antibiotic use — India में regulated नहीं है

explanation: India National Action Plan on AMR 2017-2021 (aligned with WHO Global Action Plan 2015): 6 strategic priorities: (1) Awareness & education — IEC for healthcare providers + public (no self-medication), (2) Surveillance — ICMR AMR Surveillance + Research Network (AMRSN) in 30 hospitals, (3) Infection Prevention & Control — hand hygiene, WASH, (4) Antibiotic stewardship — hospital antibiotic policy, (5) Agricultural AMR — Veterinary antibiotics, food safety (FSSAI), (6) R&D — new antibiotics, diagnostics, vaccines. Key issues: OTC antibiotic sale (Schedule H1 but poorly enforced), AYUSH-allopathy combinations, livestock growth promoters. NAP 2.0 (2022-2025) continued।

question: '15वां वित्त आयोग' (15th Finance Commission) ने स्वास्थ्य क्षेत्र को लेकर क्या विशेष प्रावधान किए?

options.text: 15th Finance Commission — health sector को specifically address नहीं किया
15th FC ने पहली बार dedicated health grant (₹70,051 crore) — States को health spend बढ़ाने की condition; Local Bodies को health SHC/PHC upgrade के लिए tied grant
15th FC — health funds केवल Central Ministry को देता है
Finance Commission — health sector की recommendation नहीं कर सकता

explanation: 15th Finance Commission (2021-26) health provisions — historic first: (1) Sector-specific grants for health: ₹70,051 crore (2021-26) to states — conditional on states increasing health expenditure to ≥8% of state budget, (2) Local body grants for health: ULBs and PRIs for SHC/HWC upgradation, sanitation, water, (3) States must publish health accounts (NHA framework), (4) Vertical fiscal imbalance: states to increase own health spending, (5) Performance grants linked to health outcomes (MMR, IMR, TFR improvement). Significance: First time FC created conditional health-specific grants — nudges states toward spending commitments. India health spending goal: 2.5% of GDP by 2025 (NHP 2017)।

question: भारत में 'Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO)' और 'State Drug Controllers' के बीच regulatory jurisdiction कैसे विभाजित है?

options.text: CDSCO — सभी drug regulation करता है, states का कोई role नहीं
CDSCO: new drug approval, import, clinical trials, biologicals; State Drug Controllers: manufacture license, distribution, retail sale, drug quality surveillance — Drugs & Cosmetics Act 1940
State Drug Controllers — केवल Ayurvedic drugs regulate करते हैं
Drug regulation — पूर्णतः Concurrent List में है

explanation: Drug Regulation in India — divided under Drugs & Cosmetics Act 1940: Central (CDSCO under MoHFW): (1) New Drug approval (IND/NDA/ANDA), (2) Import licenses, (3) Clinical trial permission, (4) Biologicals/vaccines, (5) Medical devices (CDSCO-MDCO), (6) Schedule H, H1, X drugs. State Drug Controllers: (1) Manufacturing licenses (GMP inspection), (2) Distribution, wholesale, retail licenses, (3) Drug quality testing (State Drug Testing Labs), (4) Enforcement at field level. Issue: Regulatory gap — state capacity varies, spurious/substandard drugs. Drugs (Prices Control) Order under NPPA (National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority) — MoC&I, not MoHFW. HEO: drug quality vigilance, rational drug use promotion।

question: भारत में 'RMNCH+A Strategy' (2013) का 'continuum of care' approach और HEO की क्या भूमिका है?

options.text: RMNCH+A — केवल child health program है

RMNCH+A (Reproductive Maternal Neonatal Child and Adolescent health): continuum — preconception to adolescence; convergence platform; high burden districts first; facility + community + outreach levels
RMNCH+A — replaced NHM को
RMNCH+A में Adolescent health component नहीं है

explanation: RMNCH+A Strategy 2013 (MoHFW): 'Strategic Approach to Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child and Adolescent Health.' Key features: (1) Continuum of care: preconception → pregnancy → birth → postnatal → childhood → adolescence, (2) Life-cycle approach: not vertical programs, (3) Convergence: NHM umbrella — JSY, JSSK, iMNCl, RBSK, RKSK under one framework, (4) High-burden districts (184) prioritized, (5) Three levels: household-community (ASHA, AWW), outreach (VHNDs), facility (SHC to DH), (6) '5×5 strategy matrix' — 5 interventions × 5 stages. JSSK: Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram — free delivery + newborn services. HEO coordinates all RMNCH+A components at field level।

question: भारत में 'Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP)' का governance structure और HEO की surveillance भूमिका क्या है?

options.text: IDSP — केवल epidemic situations में activate होता है

IDSP (2004): P-form (community), L-form (lab), S-form (clinician) — weekly data; District Surveillance Unit (DSU) headed by CMO/DM; HEO: field verification, outbreak investigation support, community reporting
IDSP — WHO द्वारा operate किया जाता है
IDSP data — confidential, public को available नहीं

explanation: IDSP (Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme, 2004 — World Bank funded): 3-level structure: District → State → Central. Reporting forms: P-form (Presumptive/community — ASHA, AWW — weekly), L-form (Lab confirmed), S-form (Syndromic — clinicians). District Surveillance Unit (DSU): DM + CMO as co-chairs, Epidemiologist, Microbiologist, Entomologist. Alerts: if disease doubles in 2 weeks → outbreak declaration. IHIP (Integrated Health Information Platform) — digital upgrade of IDSP (2020 COVID era). HEO role: (1) Community-level surveillance coordination, (2) Verify rumors, (3) Rapid Response Team (RRT) support, (4) IEC during outbreaks, (5) IDSP report dissemination to community health workers।

question: 'Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA)' का क्या उद्देश्य है और इसका accountability mechanism क्या है?

options.text: PMSMA — JSY का duplicate program है
PMSMA (2016): हर महीने 9 तारीख को 2nd/3rd trimester की ANC — specialist doctors (private sector volunteer), high-risk pregnancy identification, assured quality ANC, 'Happy Mother Healthy Baby' portal
PMSMA — केवल urban health facilities में
PMSMA — institutional delivery ensure करने का program है

explanation: Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA) 2016: Objective — assured, quality ANC on 9th of every month for 2nd/3rd trimester pregnancies at government facilities. Features: (1) Specialist participation: OB-GYN, physicians — government + volunteer private doctors, (2) High-risk pregnancy (HRP) identification + referral — MCP card marked in red, (3) Services: BP, weight, blood test, ultrasound, iron/folic acid, TT, (4) 'Happy Mother Healthy Baby' portal — beneficiary registration, doctor reporting, (5) PMSMA Plus (2021): first trimester coverage added. Accountability: HMIS reporting, beneficiary feedback mechanism. Different from JSY: JSY = delivery cash transfer; PMSMA = ANC quality improvement।

question: भारत में 'National Health Systems Resource Centre (NHSRC)' की क्या भूमिका है और यह NHM implementation में कैसे सहायता करता है?

options.text: NHSRC — एक financial institution है

NHSRC (2007): NHM का technical support institution — guidelines, operational research, training modules, PIP review support, HR policy, community processes, QI, HWC design; State HRCs के capacity building
NHSRC — केवल private sector health के लिए काम करता है
NHSRC — WHO की संस्था है

explanation: National Health Systems Resource Centre (NHSRC) 2007: Autonomous body under MoHFW — technical + knowledge support to NHM. Functions: (1) Policy support: NHM guidelines development (HWC, VHSNC, RKS operational guidelines), (2) Operational research: documentation of innovations, evidence generation, (3) Training: Master trainers, curricula for ASHA, ANM, MOs, (4) PIP (Programme Implementation Plan) technical review, (5) Quality Assurance: LaQshya, NQAS, Kayakalp program design, (6) Community processes: VHSNC, social audit guidelines, (7) HR policy: HRSRC (Human Resources for Health resource centre within NHSRC). State HRCs — State counterparts. NHSRC produces annual reports on community processes, HR for health。

question: 'New Education Policy 2020 (NEP 2020)' और स्वास्थ्य शिक्षा (Health Education) के बीच क्या महत्वपूर्ण संबंध हैं?

options.text: NEP 2020 — health education को address नहीं करता

NEP 2020: Foundational Literacy + Numeracy में health literacy; Vocational education में community health; Medical education — integrated curriculum; School Health Programme linkage; Life Skills education
NEP 2020 — केवल school education का framework है, health से असंबंधित
NEP 2020 ने AYUSH को medical curriculum से हटाया

explanation: NEP 2020 and Health Education: (1) Foundational stage (3-8 years): health habits, hygiene, nutrition — integrated in curriculum, (2) Vocational Education: healthcare — community health worker as vocational stream, (3) Higher Education: medical education reform — NMC coordinates, integrated curriculum, (4) School Health Programme (SHP): linkage — annual health checkup, RBSK screening, health record, (5) Life Skills education: mental health, substance abuse prevention, (6) Midday Meal + POSHAN convergence, (7) M.Sc. Public Health, MPH — included in higher education expansion vision, (8) HEO training institutionalized — BSc Community Health, (9) NEP vision: 'holistic development' — physical, mental health integral to education। Significance: HEO role in school health programs strengthened।

question: भारत में 'Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM)' का क्या उद्देश्य है और यह NHM से कैसे भिन्न है?

options.text: PM-ABHIM — NHM का ही नया नाम है

PM-ABHIM (2021, ₹64,180 crore): health infrastructure focus — HWCs, Critical Care blocks, 5000 Urban HWCs, Integrated Public Health Labs, Block/District/National institutions; NHM = service delivery; ABHIM = infrastructure
PM-ABHIM — केवल rural health infrastructure के लिए है
PM-ABHIM — insurance scheme है

explanation: PM Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM) 2021: Budget ₹64,180 crore (2021-26). Components: (1) 17,788 HWCs (rural) + 11,024 Urban HWCs, (2) Critical Care Hospital Blocks (CCBs) in district hospitals — ICU, OT, NICU, (3) Integrated Public Health Labs (IPHL) in 730 districts, (4) Block Public Health Units (BPHUs) in 3382 blocks, (5) 15 Health Emergency Operation Centres (HEOCs) — pandemic preparedness, (6) National Centre for Disease Control strengthening, (7) WHO SEARO Collaborating Centres. Difference from NHM: NHM = program funds (ASHA wages, drugs, HR); PM-ABHIM = capital infrastructure. Together: NHM provides services in PM-ABHIM-built infrastructure।

question: भारत में 'WHO-India Country Cooperation Strategy' और SDG health targets में alignment कैसे है?

options.text: WHO-India — केवल epidemic response में collaborate करते हैं
WHO-India CCS: 3 strategic priorities — Universal Health Coverage, Health Security, Healthier Populations; SDG 3 targets mapped; WHO technical support — surveillance, guidelines, training, policy
India को WHO से कोई technical support नहीं मिलती
SDG health targets — India ने adopt नहीं किए

explanation: WHO-India Country Cooperation Strategy (CCS 2019-2023, renewed 2024-2028): 3 priorities aligned with WHO Thirteenth General Programme of Work: (1) Universal Health Coverage (UHC) — PM-JAY, HWCs, human resources, (2) Health Security — IDSP, IHR, pandemic preparedness, (3) Healthier Populations — NCD prevention, nutrition, WASH, mental health. SDG 3 alignment: (1) SDG 3.1 MMR <70 (India: 97 per lakh LB, 2020), (2) SDG 3.2 U5MR <25 (India: 32, NFHS-5), (3) SDG 3.3 AIDS/TB/malaria, (4) SDG 3.8 UHC index. WHO role: normative guidance, technical review of programs, emergency response (COVID, outbreak). SEARO (South-East Asia Regional Office) — New Delhi।

question: भारत में 'State-specific Health Plans (State NHM PIPs)' बनाने की प्रक्रिया और केंद्र-राज्य संबंध में इसकी क्या भूमिका है?

options.text: States — Centre के approval के बिना अपने health programs चला सकते हैं
Annual PIP process: States prepare → District PIPs aggregate → State PIP → National NHM Program Coordination Committee review → approval + fund release; state flexibility within national norms
PIP — केवल financial document है, programmatic planning नहीं
PIP — WHO द्वारा approve किया जाता है

explanation: Programme Implementation Plan (PIP) process under NHM: (1) Bottom-up: VHSNC → Gram Panchayat → PHC → Block → District Health Action Plan (DHAP) → State PIP, (2) State PIP contents: epidemiological profile, last year performance, proposed activities, budget, HR plan, (3) National Program Coordination Committee (NPCC) at MoHFW: reviews, negotiates with states, approves, (4) Fund flow: Central share released in installments based on utilization + audit, (5) Flexibility: States can reallocate within approved budget (up to 10-15%), (6) Innovation: States can propose new interventions in 'flexible pool'. Centre-State tension: Center's approval power vs State's right to health planning. NHSRC provides technical support for PIP preparation।

question: 'Positive Deviance (PD) Approach' को भारत में health programs में कैसे लागू किया गया है?

options.text: PD Approach — India में use नहीं होता
PD Approach: community के सफल outliers (positive deviants) की practices identify करना — Rajasthan में malnutrition reduction, VHSNC best practices replication; community-owned solution
PD — top-down expert-driven intervention है
PD — Statistical outlier removal technique है

explanation: Positive Deviance (PD) Approach: Sternin concept — find 'positive deviants' (community members who succeed despite same constraints as others). India applications: (1) Rajasthan Nutrition: families with well-nourished children in poor communities — their feeding practices identified and spread, (2) Uttar Pradesh: ASHAs with better immunization coverage — their strategies shared, (3) VHSNC: high-functioning VSHNCs studied and replicated, (4) Bihar: community leaders promoting institutional delivery in conservative areas. Process: (1) Define problem, (2) Discover PD individuals, (3) Inquire PD behaviors, (4) Design community activities to share, (5) Monitor. Advantage: Community ownership, sustainability. Used in NHM community processes documentation (NHSRC)।

question: भारत में 'Health and Wellness Centres (HWCs)' के transformation में HEO की comprehensive governance भूमिका क्या है?

options.text: HWC — केवल clinical service delivery center है

HEO at HWC: comprehensive primary care 12 service packages, Community Health Officer (CHO) supervision, Jan Arogya Samiti (JAS), VHSNC linkage, HMIS data quality, community outreach, IEC coordination, quality assurance (NQAS)
HWC — Medical Officer द्वारा ही manage हो सकता है
HEO — HWC में administrative नहीं बल्कि केवल clinical role है

explanation: HEO's comprehensive role at Health and Wellness Centre (HWC/AB-HWC): (1) Service delivery coordination: 12 CPHC packages (NCDs, maternal, child, palliative, mental health, AYUSH, oral, eye, ENT, emergency), (2) Community Health Officer (CHO — B.Sc. Community Health) supervision, (3) Jan Arogya Samiti (JAS): community governance body — meetings, agenda, minutes, (4) VHSNC: village-level health + sanitation committee — coordinate monthly meetings, village health plan, (5) HMIS data quality: verify entries, correct errors, submit monthly, (6) IEC: Arogya Melas, health camps, mobile health units coordination, (7) NQAS certification: prepare HWC for quality assessment, (8) NCD screening camps: HbP, DM, cancer (CPHC focus), (9) ASHA/AWW coordination: monthly meetings, problem-solving। HEO is the backbone of community health governance।

question: भारत में 'Epidemic Diseases Amendment Act 2020' ने 1897 के original act में क्या महत्वपूर्ण बदलाव किए?

options.text: 2020 Amendment — COVID-specific था और expire हो गया

Epidemic Diseases Amendment Act 2020: healthcare workers पर attacks को criminal offense (imprisonment + fine), gender-neutral 'person' term, Central powers expand — Inspecting Officers; COVID context में enacted
2020 Amendment ने quarantine powers को cancel किया
2020 Amendment — State powers बढ़ाई, Central नहीं

explanation: Epidemic Diseases (Amendment) Act 2020: Context: COVID-19, attacks on healthcare workers. Key amendments to 1897 Act: (1) New Section 3A: Protection of healthcare service personnel — attacks, harassment, damage to property → offense, (2) Cognizable and non-bailable offenses: imprisonment 3 months-5 years + fine ₹50,000-2 lakh; grievous hurt: 6 months-7 years, ₹1-5 lakh, (3) Compensation: damage/destruction of property by attacker (2x market value), (4) Central powers: Central Government can also invoke provisions (earlier only state government), (5) Inspecting Officers: Central government can designate, (6) 'Person' gender-neutral. Limitation: Still doesn't have comprehensive health emergency framework — DM Act 2005 + Epidemic Diseases Act 1897 + 2020 remain patchwork।

question: भारत में 'Health Education Officer (HEO)' की comprehensive political-administrative role में किन क्षमताओं की आवश्यकता है?

options.text: HEO — केवल IEC material बनाता है

HEO: policy analysis (Central-State health laws), program management (NHM, RMNCH+A, NCD), community governance (VHSNC, JAS), inter-departmental coordination, surveillance (IDSP), advocacy, rights-based health approach, data-driven planning
HEO — clinical treatment भी provide करता है
HEO — District Collector के under directly काम करता है, CMO के under नहीं

explanation: Health Education Officer (HEO) — comprehensive role synthesis: (1) Policy competencies: understands Constitutional health provisions, NHM framework, DPSP Art. 47, State/Concurrent List, key health Acts (MHCA 2017, RPWD 2016, PCPNDT, COTPA), (2) Program management: NHM PIP process, RMNCH+A, NCD screening, TB program (NIKSHAY), IDSP surveillance, (3) Community governance: VHSNC, JAS, Gram Panchayat coordination, social audit, (4) IEC/BCC: evidence-based communication, SBCC, culturally sensitive messaging, (5) Data: HMIS quality, data analysis, DHAP preparation input, (6) Coordination: AWW, ASHA, PHC staff, Block, District, NGOs, PRIs, (7) Rights-based: address health inequities, SC/ST/PWD/mental health rights, (8) Accountability: RTI compliance, grievance redressal support. HEO = link between community and health system।

question: भारत में 'National Health Mission' के अंतर्गत 'Village Health, Sanitation and Nutrition Committee (VHSNC)' की संरचना और कार्य क्या हैं?

options.text: VHSNC — केवल sanitation का काम करती है
VHSNC: 15 सदस्य (ward member, ASHA, AWW, educated youth, महिला, SC/ST प्रतिनिधि) — ग्राम स्तरीय स्वास्थ्य योजना, untied fund ₹10,000, जवाबदेही और सामुदायिक स्वास्थ्य निगरानी
VHSNC — केवल Gram Panchayat सदस्यों से मिलकर बनती है
VHSNC — District Hospital स्तर पर होती है
